solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Patiently gutted, turned and stuffed fish to go round

indicators.note: stuffed means filled, so the fish has the other piece packed inside it

parts.note: the bass is a fish

indicators.note: turned tells us the extracted pair is read backwards
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: prepare the fish patiently, gutting and stuffing it, then serve it to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patiently gutted' leaves PY; 'turned' makes YP, which is stuffed into BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to avoid it by going round it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Commotion broken up, halved by wall

indicators.note: halved asks for the first half of each of the two words

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken wall or ditch bounding a park

explanation.surface: A disturbance broken up and split in two by a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of 'broken' is BRO and half of 'up' is U. A ha-ha is a sunken boundary wall in an English country garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Is a tropical storm suitable for fishing?

indicators.note: a storm throws everything into disorder, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: Asking whether tropical storm weather is good for going fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Piscatorial is a formal adjective meaning relating to fishing or anglers.

clue.text: Check prisoner's accommodation that is capable of differentiation

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check it
a prisoner is lodged in a cell

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a prisoner's quarters to see whether they can be told apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Biology: an undifferentiated cell that can develop into many specialised types.

clue.text: Hot rock and roll orchestra, rhythm group finally part of the sixties scene

parts.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A rock'n'roll band's line-up evokes the music of the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot rock and roll' looks like a music phrase, but 'Hot rock' is the volcanic piece and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamp of bubbling coloured wax, invented in 1963, is an icon of sixties decor.

clue.text: Miscellaneous crass or tedious contents

indicators.note: contents says the answer lies inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of rude or boring material.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted and miscellaneous both mean of various kinds, mixed.

clue.text: Corrupt blue period gets blanket coverage at last

parts.note: blue films are adult, that is pornographic
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A shady phase of pornography gets saturation media coverage in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to corrupt or debase something by adding impurities.

clue.text: We sue a friend, he waves goodbye

indicators.note: waves suggests motion back and forth, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man waves farewell after being taken to court by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he waves goodbye' looks like the definition, but 'he' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The German phrase is the usual way to say farewell, until we meet again.

clue.text: Raven author's attempt, perhaps

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote The Raven
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An attempt by the writer of The Raven might be verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raven is a famous poem, so Poe's effort is an example of verse.

clue.text: Cover version's vitality

indicators.note: the apostrophe s stands for has: the words have the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A remake of a song shows real energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve is energy and enthusiasm, a synonym for vitality.

clue.text: Boob, half visible, said to be lewd

indicators.note: half asks for one half of the word, here its second pair of letters
said indicates a word that sounds like the synonym, not its spelling

parts.note: visible means seen

explanation.surface: A gaffe, or a partly exposed body, is reported as indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the back half of 'Boob' is used: OB. SEEN said aloud gives SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene and lewd are synonyms for indecent or offensive material.

clue.text: Hundred abandon fight for love of a dish

indicators.note: abandon tells us one letter leaves the word for fight
for says another letter takes the departed one's place

parts.note: a scuffle is a brief fight
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A centenarian gives up fighting in favour of a love of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: In SCUFFLE the C (hundred) is replaced by O (love).
explanation.definitionFit: A souffle is a light baked dish of whisked egg whites.

clue.text: Fool in house is useless with a kiss

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An idiot at home is no good, even with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is useless with' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to trick them, which is what a hoax does.

clue.text: I've to worry about seclusion

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frets that they have reason to worry about being isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is an idiom for a state of detachment from the practical world.

clue.text: See 7
Murder victim's nothing if sweet

definitions.meaning: a girl murdered in Hampshire in 1867, whose name became naval slang for tinned meat
with sweet in front, the phrase is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet Fanny Adams' (or 'sweet FA') is British slang for nothing; the original was a child murdered in Alton in 1867.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim's name is used in the British idiom meaning absolutely nothing.

clue.text: What follows hips swaying in here's a bunch of toffs

parts.note: the cheer goes hip hip, then the word that follows

indicators.note: swaying suggests movement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up as hips sway in a dance venue full of posh people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for loud, upper-class young men; toffs are posh people.

clue.text: See 16
Cosy hint

definitions.meaning: cosy here means warm, private and personal
hint here is a verb, to suggest indirectly

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means cosy and personal; as a verb it means to suggest.

clue.text: Sportswear-bound workers

parts.note: to bound is to leap or skip
worker ants are the crossword's usual workers

explanation.surface: Labourers who are destined to wear sports gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sportswear-bound' reads as one word, but it splits: the definition, then 'bound' for SKIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are trousers worn for skiing, an item of sportswear.

clue.text: Shallow end to life in metaphor: "long journey including a good run"

indicators.note: end to asks for the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a long life is figuratively called a good innings, from cricket

indicators.note: including means the trek takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: a trek is a long, arduous journey

explanation.surface: A writer frets about a shallow ending to a life story with a long-journey metaphor.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings is a batsman's turn at the crease; 'a good innings' means a long life.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of consecutive victories is a good run of success.

clue.text: See 20
One does not treat kindly a queen seen on public transport

parts.note: a bus is public transport
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A queen is spotted riding a bus, and she is not treated kindly.
explanation.definitionFit: An abuser is someone who mistreats others.

clue.text: Fight criminal partition

definitions.meaning: to fight with swords in sport
a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to fight with swords, a receiver of stolen goods, and a barrier.

clue.text: Stop short an off-side that's divided

parts.note: to balk is to stop short and refuse to go on

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A football commentator's halting remark about an offside call that split opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-side' looks like one football word, but 'off' scrambles SIDE into ISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Balkanised means split into small, often hostile, states or factions, after the Balkans.

clue.text: Press VIP regularly to respond to invitation

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A journalist urges an important guest to reply to an invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: The French abbreviation printed on invitations asks the guest to reply.

clue.text: See 3
Some musicians met an acclaimed composer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of players met a famous composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was a Czech composer, best known for Ma vlast.

clue.text: Arpeggio section needed in 11

indicators.note: section means a part cut from inside the word

explanation.surface: A piece of a musical run is needed in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is the answer to 11 across, a whisked dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten egg whites are an essential ingredient of the dish at 11.

clue.text: Duplicated revolutionary end to invasion of republic

indicators.note: duplicated means the piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: end to picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A revolutionary repeated, ending an invasion of a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: The republic is Chechnya, in Russia; the adjective describes things from there.
explanation.definitionFit: Chechen is the adjective meaning from or belonging to the Chechen Republic.

clue.text: Record is kept in regret, being semi-retired

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the first half of the word regret, left as it is

indicators.note: semi-retired says that half of the word is turned back, here its second half

parts.note: the second half of the word regret, the part that is turned round

explanation.surface: A record is preserved in someone's regret at only half retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-retired' reverses the last half of REGRET to make REGTER; IS goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official record or list, as a class register.

clue.text: Trees from Naples

indicators.note: from tells us these letters are made from the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Trees brought from the Italian city of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a common tree, much planted in city streets.
